entities.name: HIV-1 Env gp160
observations: The 768-aa query sequence matches reviewed HIV-1 group M envelope glycoprotein gp160 homologs at 75.6–78.0% identity with approximately 99–100% query coverage and E-value 0.

The precursor contains an N-terminal signal peptide, a heavily glycosylated cysteine-rich gp120 ectodomain, a furin-cleavage region, gp41 heptad-repeat/fusion regions, a transmembrane segment, and a short cytoplasmic tail.
Pfam detects GP120 (PF00516) at positions 33–511 and GP41 (PF00517) at positions 530–720.
The precursor is processed in the trans-Golgi by furin or furin-like proteases into gp120 and gp41; mature Env forms a trimeric gp120-gp41 spike.
Env mediates virion attachment to CD4 and subsequent engagement of CCR5 or CXCR4, followed by class-I viral membrane fusion.

Localization is the virion envelope and host-cell/endosomal membranes; it is a type I membrane glycoprotein with the large ectodomain exposed externally and the C-terminal tail inside the virion/cell.
Sequence-derived properties: 768 aa, approximately 86.4 kDa unmodified mass, theoretical pI 8.75, and predicted positive charge at neutral pH.

entities.name: HIV-1 gp120 domain
observations: Pfam GP120 (PF00516.25) is detected in the query at residues 33–511 with i-Evalue 3.6e-188.
The region is cysteine-rich and contains many potential N-linked glycosylation sequons, consistent with the receptor-binding exterior subunit of HIV Env.

entities.name: HIV-1 gp41 domain
observations: Pfam GP41 (PF00517.23) is detected in the query at residues 530–720 with i-Evalue 7e-44.
This region contains the fusion-associated heptad-repeat/coiled-coil segment and the membrane anchor characteristic of the transmembrane Env subunit.

entities.name: HIV host-cell entry
observations: Env attachment to CD4 induces exposure or formation of a coreceptor-binding site for CCR5 or CXCR4 and enables viral entry.
The gp41 fusion machinery drives fusion of viral and host endosomal or plasma membranes, delivering the viral core into the cytoplasm.
